# BTicino C300X Integration v2.2.0

## 2026-11-14

This release expands the native display, reorganizes its settings and combines
the reliability and security fixes reviewed since 2.1.3.

## Native Display

- Settings open as independent areas for connection, media, activations,
  Alarmo, the display, pages and tiles. Each tile has a section with its size,
  name and secondary line; fields include translated labels and help text.
- Page names and connection status move into the display header, leaving more
  space for tiles. Configure up to eight ordered pages. Weather heads the
  status page; Alarmo and its optional quick action have their own setup step.
- Add locks, vacuums, valves, humidifiers and water heaters with the controls
  their entities support. Unlocking or opening a lock asks for a second tap;
  leaving the page or sleeping the display clears that question.
- Automations and sirens are switch tiles; people and device trackers are
  read-only tiles. Type symbols and short local timestamps improve scanning.
- Media controls share a compact button row, show the artist, and offer
  shuffle and repeat when supported. Lights can expose effects; fan steps
  follow the fan's speed grid.
- Optional dashboard fields can be cleared reliably. Queued commands expire
  on timeout or page exit, and alarm state refreshes after concurrent events.
- Display files are smaller without changing their intended behaviour.

## Reliability and Security

- Handle malformed webhook credentials and failed setup without leaving
  registrations behind. Discovery cannot silently redirect saved credentials;
  confirm device-address changes through Reconfigure.
- Preserve customized obsolete blueprints, pending configuration changes and
  unfinished display-update follow-up across retries.
- Preserve device-owned configuration during SSH reinstalls and sync saved
  configuration, installed update files and private SIP account files before
  publishing them. Routing restoration accepts only a verified stock backup.
- Reserve HTTP client capacity for the local display, limit unauthenticated
  RTSP connections and clear inbound SRTP keys when on-demand sessions end.
- Bound Wyoming transcription time and data size, clean up failed recordings,
  and keep a late talkback keepalive failure from invalidating a finished clip.
- Reject non-finite numbers, malformed addresses and unsafe memo/message IDs.
  Keep token fingerprints admin-only and report repair failures in the log.
- Refresh message details before deleting the latest item. Validate extracted
  capture images against the actual video duration and clear missing aliases.
- Cancel media setup when stopped, reclaim completed workers and partially
  initialized SRTP sessions, and keep slow RTSP clients from blocking writes
  indefinitely. Device-media renewal no longer runs in the audio worker.
- Scope RTSP probe failures to their request and stop automatic preview retry
  loops after an error. A new ring can try again.
- Validate configured RTSP credentials and SDES key selection. RTSP supports
  TCP interleaving only; UDP requests now receive an explicit rejection instead
  of being accepted without working UDP delivery. HA already uses TCP.
- Bound mDNS query processing, preserve queued MQTT commands and handle partial
  HTTP requests and responses safely. See [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md) for
  the device's remaining local-network and transport limitations.
- Validate release archive contents against the checkout before generating
  metadata or adopting draft assets. Local installation and patch-copy helpers
  now stop safely on copy errors or conflicting source/output paths.

## Upgrade

- **Update the native agent to 2.2.0** using the offered Repair after updating
  the integration. This release includes a rebuilt agent and new display files;
  updating only Home Assistant does not apply the device-side fixes.
- Reapplying an active Display patch restarts the device GUI once.
- Home Assistant **2026.7.0** remains the minimum. Existing integration entries
  and card configurations can be kept.
- Native behaviour is checked with host regression tests, sanitizers and an
  ARMHF build. Display tests use source contracts and a JavaScript harness,
  not the device's Qt runtime. No new hardware validation is claimed.
